newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to sign contract with Turkey for gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to sign contract with Turkey for gas pipeline.

text.p: Iraq will discuss with Turkey by end December a contract for a natural gas pipeline between the two countries, Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
"We will discuss with Turkey at the end of this month a gas pipeline project in order to sign a contract," Rasheed said in press remarks published by the official al-Thawra newspaper.
The Minister gave no more details on the contract, its cost or how Iraq would pay to build the pipeline.

Both countries agreed last August to set up the pipeline during a visit to Iraq by Turkey's Justice Minister Sevket Kazan and Education Minister Mehmet Saglam. They put the designed capacity of the pipeline at 10 billion cubic metres a year.

Rasheed said Iraq began producing large quantities of gas since it started last week oil exports within the oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations on May 20. "We want to export liquid gas (to world markets) through the Arab Gulf and Turkey," he said.

Iraq on Tuesday began oil exports worth $2 billion over six months under the deal to buy humanitarian needs for its people, suffering from stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Rasheed made his remarks while he was visiting Basra to supervise government celebrations to mark the start of exports from Gulf terminals for the first time since the sanctions were imposed.
He said the Oil Ministry was "planning to improve oilfields relying on local know-how and on multi-national oil companies specialised on this sphere."
